cases.purpose: FIFO operands terminate without a peer or with a reader; report fsync failure, close descriptors, and continue to a later regular file.
cases.oracle: Linux FIFO nonblocking open and fsync semantics in the disposable guest
cases.comparison: Exact stdout and empty stderr; watchdog detects blocking, captured diagnostic names FIFO, and a later regular operand succeeds in the same process.
cases.script:
exec 9<>pace.fifo
( sync pipe.fifo 2>fifo.err; printf 'fifo-status=%d\n' "$?"; sync later.txt; printf 'later-status=%d\n' "$?" ) >result.txt &
p=$!
for ((i=0; i<100; i++)); do
  line=; { read -r line <"/proc/$p/stat"; } 2>/dev/null || break
  a=(${line##*) }); [[ ${a[0]} == Z ]] && break
  read -r -t 0.02 -u 9 _ || :
done
if [[ -e /proc/$p ]] && { read -r line <"/proc/$p/stat"; a=(${line##*) }); [[ ${a[0]} != Z ]]; } 2>/dev/null; then
  builtin kill -KILL "$p"; wait "$p" 2>/dev/null; printf 'fifo=blocked\n'
else
  wait "$p"; printf 'fifo=returned\n'; while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s\n' "$line"; done <result.txt
fi
IFS= read -r line <fifo.err; [[ $line == *pipe.fifo* ]] && printf 'diagnostic=named\n' || printf 'diagnostic=missing\n'
exec 8<>pipe.fifo
sync pipe.fifo 2>fifo-reader.err
printf 'fifo-with-reader-status=%d\n' "$?"
exec 8>&-
